title: finding(spec): the expression dialect table lists notification subjects/bodies as `template` slots, but NotifyConfigSchema.title is z.string() and refuses the tmpl envelope
body:
Found by the `repo:objectos` seat (objectstack-ai/objectstack#9831) while staging objectos#316, the docs code-sample gate, on 2026-10-07. Measured on the published `@objectstack/spec` 17.7.0 and read at `origin/main`. **Class b:** the contract text and the schema disagree.

## What disagrees

- **`packages/spec/src/shared/expression.zod.ts:27`.** The dialect table names the `template` dialect's slots as "notification subjects/bodies, `titleFormat`, prompt templates". A template-typed slot accepts either a bare string or the `{ dialect: 'template', source }` envelope (`TemplateExpressionInputSchema`, `:36`, and the guidance at `:292-295`).
- **`packages/spec/src/automation/io-node-config.zod.ts:192`.** `NotifyConfigSchema.title` is `z.string().optional()`, so only a bare string parses.
- **Effect.** A notify node written with the `tmpl` helper is refused, by `defineFlow` and by `NotifyConfigSchema` alike: `title: expected string, received object`. Example: `` title: tmpl`[{{record.priority}}] {{record.subject}}` ``. The bare-string spelling of the same text parses.

## Why it matters

Docs and authors who follow the dialect table write the envelope form for notifications and get a schema error. objectos's `reference/cel.mdx` now follows the parse, using bare strings for notify titles, after objectos#316 / PR #321.

## Possible directions (the owner decides)

- Type `NotifyConfigSchema.title`, and any body or subject field, as `TemplateExpressionInputSchema`, so both spellings parse. Or:
- Correct the dialect table row so it no longer promises the envelope for notification subjects and bodies.

Either way, a test pinning the decision closes it.
